rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.subtype: Approach: going along to avoid being excluded [Pitfall]
rows.description: Worried about being called boring, the student joins a risky dare. The fear of social loss feels larger than the real danger in that moment, and the consequences fall on him alone.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: inversion, prioritising, values-first planning
related mind states: anger, fear, anxiety

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.subtype: Approach: humour or redirect to another activity [Action]
rows.description: The student jokes it off and proposes cricket or a movie instead. Offering a substitute often lets others save face and shift too, since several may not really want to do it either.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, inversion, prioritising, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.description: The student imagines what happens if the dare goes wrong: injury, school action, a call to parents. Seeing the worst case beside the short thrill makes the choice clearer.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, prioritising, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.subtype: Approach: leaving the situation and telling a trusted adult [Action]
rows.description: When the pressure continues, the student walks out, calls a parent or an uncle, and later tells the school counsellor about the dangerous plan, prioritising safety over group loyalty.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, inversion, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.subtype: Approach: assuming everyone else is comfortable [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student thinks all others want to do it and stays silent. Later he learns that several felt uneasy too, showing how a false belief in group agreement keeps everyone quiet.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, inversion, prioritising, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.subtype: Approach: finding an ally in the group [Action]
rows.description: By quietly asking one friend if she is comfortable, the student finds support, and two people declining together makes it far easier to say no than standing alone.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, inversion, prioritising, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.description: After a risky evening the student admits it was a mistake, tells his parents what happened, and plans different company, earlier exit times and a firm rule for next time rather than hiding it.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: inversion, prioritising, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.description: Noticing that certain friends repeatedly pressure him and mock refusal, the student spends more time with others who respect limits, keeping a friendly but distant tone with the pushy group.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, inversion, prioritising, values-first planning

rows.description: The teenager asks why parents refuse late evenings out and learns the concerns are safety and late-night travel, not distrust, which allows a plan that addresses those specific concerns.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, negotiation, values-first planning

rows.description: The teen proposes going to a friend's house until 8 pm, sharing the address and location, phoning on arrival and being picked up by a parent, offering a trial for a month.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, values-first planning
